newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - March 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - March 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following a day of looting and angry demonstrations in Port Moresby yesterday and unrest in the Papua New Guinea Defence Force, Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan has announced his Cabinet would consider cancelling their Sandline contract and admitted for the first time the plan to hire mercenaries to ease the conflict on Bougainville might have been badly timed. The move comes as Australia looks set to offer increased military aid to PNG to enable it to stop using the mercenaries. Page 1.

Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge will hold a series of meetings next week with specialist medical colleges to pressure them to change the "closed shop" control of the number of places offered and offer more spots to young doctors, or face full srutiny by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission. Page 3.

National Party Leader Tim Fischer and Nationals Federal president Don McDonald have supported a move by backbenchers to demand the Federal Government extinguish Aboriginal native title over pastoral leases. The move comes after the High Court found the two could co-exist in its controversial Wik ruling. Page 3.

According to the leading index of economic activity prepared by Westpac and the Melbourne Institute, which shows where economic activity is likely to be in six to nine months, economic growth will be close to four percent by the end of 1997 with the index rising one percent in January. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In the first indication of a turnaround on his controversial plan to send foreign mercenaries to Bougainville, Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan admitted last night he might have been wrong and agreed to meet three special Australian envoys to discuss means of resolving the crisis. The comments came after a day of civilian rioting in Port Moresby. Page 1.

Just days before Prime Minister John Howard is due to visit China in the hope of repairing a strained relationship, Taiwan Foreign Affairs Minister John Chang has criticised Australia for its failure to adequately explain a temporary halt to ministerial visits - a move which has been welcomed by Beijing. Page 1.

The early retirement from the High Court of Justice Daryl Dawson, 63, expected to leave the bench in mid-August, will give the Federal Government more opportunity to shape the court at a time of unusual tension between the political and judicial branches. Sir Daryl's retirement will speed up the judgment in two pivotal cases heard by the bench under Chief Justice Sir Gerard Brennan. Page 1.

Democrats environment spokeswoman Senator Meg Lees yesterday pledged the party's support for the A$1.25 million Natural Heritage Trust Fund Bill after the Federal Government agreed to include 18 amendments hoped to increase the accountability for the allocation of trust funds. The pledge of support has assured the delivery of the trust. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As Prime Minister John Howard yesterday sent senior diplomatic and defence officials to Papua New Guinea to discuss an Australian-led peace process for the Bougainville crisis, Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan said six mercenaries had alreay been sent out of the country, indicating he is wavering on his controversial plan to use foreign mercenaries on the strife-torn island. The move came after a day of angry street protests in the capital, Port Moresby. Page 1.

Amid intense public outrage about possible detrimental effects on the Opera House from an apartments complex on the southern end of East Circular Quay, the owner of the main site, Hong Kong and Shanghai Hotels, has revealed it is rethinking the future of the site. Page 1.

The Supreme Court yesterday acquitted Glenda Lillian Lock, 45, of both murder and an alternative charge of manslaughter after she killed her abusive de facto husband, John Hume McMahon, at their Seven Hills home. Records tendered at the trail showed that Lock was admitted to hospital six times between May 1989 and March 1994 with various injuries. Page 1.

In a move which indicates the Federal Government has abandoned its plan to find full-time work for Australia's 810,000 unemployed, the Coalition has announced that it will regard people who work 20 hours a week as having a full-time job under its radical hake-up of JobSearch assistance. Page 1.
THE AGE

According to an internal memo obtained by the Victorian Opposition under the Freedom of Information Act, the Metropolitan Ambulance Service's contract with the Intergraph computer dispatch system has been secretly boosted by almost A$30 million in two years. Page 1.

According to a leaked document from the Local Authorities Superannuation Board, presented in Parliament yesterday by the Victorian Opposition, newly elected councils are facing a A$330 million black hole in unfunded superannuation liabilities due to wide-ranging retrenchments by the State Government's Local Government commissioners. Page 1.

The managers of superannuation funds, which have been driving much new investment, warned yesterday Victoria will lose significant funds for large infrastructure projects as an unintended consequence of the federal super surcharge, which they believe will hit many low-income earners as well as the wealthy. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
